title: TikTok: 10,000 bitcoin for two pizzas (map + Sam + detailed coded scenes + chart)
_sources:
TikTok "10,000 bitcoin for two pizzas" (Bitcoin Pizza Day) -> project.json
Sources (checked 2026-10-27):
Nasdaq "Happy Bitcoin Pizza Day": 22 May 2010, Florida programmer Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 BTC for two Papa John's pizzas, worth ~$41 then;
  widely regarded as the first real-world purchase with bitcoin; celebrated yearly on 22 May as Bitcoin Pizza Day.
BTC-Echo "10.000 Bitcoin fuer zwei Pizzen – was wurde aus Laszlo Hanyecz?": Jacksonville, Florida; request posted in a bitcoin forum, accepted 22 May 2010.
BitcoinTalk thread "Pizza for bitcoins?" (18 May 2010): "a couple of pizzas.. like maybe 2 large ones".
Price: CoinGecko via Analytics Insight 27.10.2026: 1 BTC = $79,769.40 -> 10,000 BTC = $797.7M (~"about eight hundred million"); 797.7M / 41 = 19.5 million times.

lines.text: This man paid almost eight hundred million dollars for two pizzas.
In May twenty-ten, a programmer in Florida posted an offer on a bitcoin forum.
Ten thousand bitcoin for two large pizzas. Back then, that was about forty-one dollars.
Four days later, someone took the deal, and two Papa John's pizzas arrived at his door.
It's seen as the first time anyone bought real goods with bitcoin.
But here's the crazy part. Today, those ten thousand bitcoin are worth about eight hundred million dollars.
That's more than nineteen million times what he paid.
And every year on May twenty-second, people celebrate it as Bitcoin Pizza Day.
